root_cause.text: In the DRM/msm VM_BIND UNMAP path, `vm_bind_job_lock_objects()` passed `op->obj_offset` to `drm_gpuvm_sm_unmap_exec_lock()` instead of the UNMAP range (`op->range`), so the exec-locking code did not always lock the GEM objects involved in UNMAP operations, creating a locking omission for non-`_NO_SHARE` BOs.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the UNMAP call in `drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_gem_vma.c` from `drm_gpuvm_sm_unmap_exec_lock(job->vm, exec, op->iova, op->obj_offset);` to `... op->range);`, and the commit message explicitly says “Wrong argument meant that the objs involved in UNMAP ops were not always getting locked” and that it only affected non-`_NO_SHARE` BOs.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix vm_bind unmap handling to pass the correct range value to drm_gpuvm_sm_unmap_exec_lock().
intent_record.what: In the UNMAP case of vm_bind_job_lock_objects(), the argument passed to drm_gpuvm_sm_unmap_exec_lock() was changed from op->obj_offset to op->range.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the unmap operation will now use the range field rather than the object offset field when locking and processing GPU VM unmap execution, which changes the address/span information supplied to the unmap helper.

grouping_result.intent: Fix vm_bind unmap handling to pass the correct range value to drm_gpuvm_sm_unmap_exec_lock().

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the root cause: it fixes vm_bind UNMAP locking by passing the correct UNMAP range to drm_gpuvm_sm_unmap_exec_lock() instead of obj_offset, addressing the locking omission.

This is the incorrect value passed to drm_gpuvm_sm_unmap_exec_lock() before the fix. The root cause states obj_offset was used instead of the UNMAP range, leading to incomplete locking of GEM objects.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is present only if the UNMAP exec-lock path passes the wrong range/offset relationship. In this snippet, `vm_bind_job_lock_objects()` handles UNMAP with `drm_gpuvm_sm_unmap_exec_lock(job->vm, exec, op->iova, op->obj_offset);`. That is indeed using `op->obj_offset` rather than `op->range`, matching the root cause. However, this commit is the initial introduction of VM_BIND, and the shown code does not contain any corrective handling for the bug (there is no alternate use of `op->range` in the UNMAP lock call, and no special-case fix for non-_NO_SHARE BOs). Therefore the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is absent.
